Crossing and equality: a_h averages a growing list of nondecreasing nonnegative drops, while b_h strictly decreases. In the interior crossing case the four cross-comparisons show the displayed interval is nonempty, and monotonicity gives betweenness at every index; the endpoint cases choose a_m or b_1. The strict surplus regime gives equality only at an unchanged radius for any slope satisfying betweenness, so equality in the sum forces an affine original profile. Conversely an affine original profile can use its original slope.

Convex realization: the interpolated slope list is the nonnegative drops in reverse order, followed by zero, followed by the nonpositive drops in forward order. It is nonincreasing, with a positive central plateau on [0,1]. The inequality on the sum of coordinates with that concave radius therefore defines a compact convex body with nonempty interior and exactly the listed integer sections, even at a zero endpoint. With m = 0 it realizes the unchanged two fibers.
